    Ported from TauCeti (TauCeti.RepresentationTheory.Quiver.Reflection.Source.Basic, commit 580b6f9d5, Apache 2.0).

    Reflecting a representation at a source #

    This file constructs the source-side Bernstein--Gelfand--Ponomarev reflection functor. For a source i, the linear map

    Mᵢ → ∏_{a : i ⟶ b} M_b

    collects the actions of all arrows leaving i. The reflected representation agrees with M away from i, replaces Mᵢ by the cokernel of this map, and lets a reversed arrow act by inserting its coordinate and passing to the quotient. The construction is functorial because a morphism of representations gives a commuting square of outgoing maps.

    The target is the product over the arrows leaving i, not a direct sum: a linear map into a direct sum must produce finitely supported families, which need not hold when infinitely many arrows leave i, whereas the arrow actions always assemble into a map to the product. Over a finite quiver the product and direct sum agree by DirectSum.linearEquivFunOnFintype, so LargeIndecomposable.Foundations.outgoingMap is then the direct-sum map Mᵢ → ⨁_{a : i ⟶ b} M_b of the BGP construction. The arrow-count and dimension-vector results below therefore carry the relevant finiteness hypotheses.

    When the outgoing map is injective, the quotient dimension is the simple reflection of the old dimension vector. This is the dual of the surjectivity condition on LargeIndecomposable.Foundations.incomingSum in the sink-side construction.

    Main definitions #

    • LargeIndecomposable.Foundations.outgoingMap: the map collecting all arrows out of a vertex.
    • LargeIndecomposable.Foundations.sourceReflectRep: reflection of a representation at a source.
    • LargeIndecomposable.Foundations.sourceReflectionFunctor: the BGP reflection functor at a source.

    Main results #

    • LargeIndecomposable.Foundations.sourceReflectRep_obj_self and LargeIndecomposable.Foundations.sourceReflectRep_obj_of_ne compute the vertex spaces.
    • LargeIndecomposable.Foundations.sourceReflectRep_map_reflectArrowSource computes the action of a reversed arrow.
    • LargeIndecomposable.Foundations.sourceReflectionFunctor_map_app_self_mk computes reflection on morphisms at the reflected vertex.
    • LargeIndecomposable.Foundations.sourceReflectionFunctor_additive records that source reflection is additive.
    • LargeIndecomposable.Foundations.outgoingMap_not_injective shows that the injectivity hypothesis below is not automatic: it fails at the vertex simple.
    • LargeIndecomposable.Foundations.dimVector_sourceReflectRep identifies the new dimension vector with the simple reflection when the outgoing map is injective.
    • LargeIndecomposable.Foundations.finiteDimensional_sourceReflectRep_obj shows that source reflection preserves finite-dimensional vertex spaces.

    References #

    See Bernstein--Gelfand--Ponomarev, Coxeter functors and Gabriel's theorem, and Derksen--Weyman, An Introduction to Quiver Representations, Ch. 2. The formal template for this dual construction is the sink-side API in LargeIndecomposable.Foundations.RepresentationTheory.Quiver.Reflection.Representation, especially LargeIndecomposable.Foundations.incomingSum, LargeIndecomposable.Foundations.reflectRep, and LargeIndecomposable.Foundations.reflectionFunctor.

    The outgoing map #

    source
    noncomputable def LargeIndecomposable.Foundations.outgoingMap {k : Type u} {Q : Type v} [Field k] [Quiver Q] (M : QuiverRep k Q) (i : Q) :
    ↑(M.obj i) →ₗ[k] (e : (b : Q) × (i ⟶ b)) → ↑(M.obj e.fst)

    The map collecting the arrows out of a vertex. Its coordinate at e : i ⟶ b is the action of e, so this is the product of the arrow actions over the arrows leaving i; for a finite quiver that product is the direct sum of the BGP construction. No hypothesis on i is imposed: the map is defined at every vertex, and it is the reflection that needs i to be a source. Its range is quotiented out in LargeIndecomposable.Foundations.sourceReflectRep.

      (outgoingMap M i) y e = (ModuleCat.Hom.hom (M.map e.snd.toPath)) y

      The coordinate of LargeIndecomposable.Foundations.outgoingMap at an arrow is the action of that arrow.

      source
      theorem LargeIndecomposable.Foundations.outgoingMap_not_injective {k : Type u} {Q : Type v} [Field k] [Quiver Q] (M : QuiverRep k Q) (i : Q) (h : ∀ (b : Q) (a : i ⟶ b), Subsingleton ↑(M.obj b)) (hne : Nontrivial ↑(M.obj i)) :
      ¬Function.Injective ⇑(outgoingMap M i)

      The map collecting the arrows out of i need not be injective. It fails to be whenever every vertex space at the target of an arrow out of i vanishes while the space at i does not, which is what the vertex simple Sᵢ does at a source: no arrow out of a source is a loop, so Sᵢ vanishes at every target of such an arrow. This is why the injectivity hypothesis of LargeIndecomposable.Foundations.dimVector_sourceReflectRep cannot be dropped.

      source
      theorem LargeIndecomposable.Foundations.finrank_pi_outgoing {k : Type u} {Q : Type v} [Field k] [Quiver Q] [Fintype Q] [(a b : Q) → Fintype (a ⟶ b)] (M : QuiverRep k Q) (i : Q) (hM : ∀ (e : (b : Q) × (i ⟶ b)), FiniteDimensional k ↑(M.obj e.fst)) :
      Module.finrank k ((e : (b : Q) × (i ⟶ b)) → ↑(M.obj e.fst)) = ∑ b : Q, Fintype.card (i ⟶ b) * Module.finrank k ↑(M.obj b)

      The target of LargeIndecomposable.Foundations.outgoingMap has dimension ∑_b #(i ⟶ b) · dim M_b.

      The reflected representation and functor #

      source
      noncomputable def LargeIndecomposable.Foundations.sourceReflectRep {k : Type u} {Q : Type v} [Field k] [Quiver Q] (M : QuiverRep k Q) {i : Q} (hi : Quiver.IsSource i) :
      QuiverRep k (Quiver.Reflect Q i)

      The reflection of a representation at a source i. It agrees with M away from i and puts the cokernel of LargeIndecomposable.Foundations.outgoingMap M i at i.
